papers.title: Isolation and characterization of a clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 H5N1 virus from dairy cattle in Wisconsin
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) (HPAI H5N1) viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b have recently been detected in U.S. dairy cattle following multiple spillover events from avian reservoirs. In December 2025, HPAI H5N1 virus was identified in a dairy herd in Wisconsin through the National Milk Testing Strategy. Here, we report the isolation of a clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype D1.1 H5N1 virus, A/dairy cow/Wisconsin/25G05743-001/2025 (WI5743-H5N1), from bulk milk associated with the affected herd, describe its phylogenetic relationships, and assess its pathogenicity in mice. Infectious virus was recovered following blind passage in embryonated chicken eggs. Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that WI5743-H5N1 is distinct from previously reported D1.1 viruses detected in dairy cattle in Nevada and Arizona, supporting an independent introduction into cattle, and indicating a likely local avian source. Compared with closely related avian viruses, WI5743-H5N1 encoded the mammalian-adapting substitution PB2-E627K and additional amino acid differences in HA, PB1-F2, and NS1. In mice, WI5743-H5N1 replicated efficiently in respiratory tissues and was detectable in the brain but exhibited lower lethality relative to other recent clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13 viruses. Together, these findings highlight the genetic and phenotypic diversity of HPAI H5N1 viruses infecting dairy cattle and underscore the importance of continued surveillance and functional characterization of emerging strains. IMPORTANCE Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses have recently entered U.S. dairy cattle through multiple spillover events from avian reservoirs, creating new opportunities for viral adaptation in mammals. Here, we describe the isolation and characterization of a clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype D1.1 H5N1 virus from bulk milk collected during a spillover event in Wisconsin in December 2025. Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated that this virus represents an independent introduction into dairy cattle distinct from previously reported D1.1 viruses identified in Nevada and Arizona. Although the virus encoded the mammalian-adapting PB2-E627K substitution, it exhibited comparatively low lethality in mice, highlighting the complexity of mammalian adaptation and pathogenicity in H5N1 viruses. These findings expand current understanding of the genetic and phenotypic diversity of H5N1 viruses infecting dairy cattle and emphasize the importance of continued surveillance and functional characterization of emerging strains.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高致病性禽流感 A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒最近从禽类 储存宿主 传播到美国奶牛中,引发了人们对哺乳动物适应和公共卫生风险的担忧。该研究旨在表征从威斯康星州奶牛群中新分离出的 H5N1 病毒,以了解其遗传和表型特性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究从 2025 年 12 月从威斯康星州奶牛群收集的散装牛奶中分离并鉴定了分支 2.3.4.4b、基因型 D1.1 H5N1 病毒(A/奶牛/威斯康星州/25G05743-001/2025)。
elements_zh.methods: 通过在含胚鸡蛋中盲传代来回收传染性病毒。确定了系统发育关系,并评估了该病毒的哺乳动物适应性取代和对小鼠的致病性。
elements_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析显示,WI5743-H5N1 与之前报道的内华达州和亚利桑那州奶牛中的 D1.1 病毒不同,表明可能是从当地鸟类来源独立引入的。该病毒编码了适应哺乳动物的 PB2-E627K 取代以及 HA、PB1-F2 和 NS1 中的其他氨基酸差异。在小鼠中,WI5743-H5N1 在呼吸组织中有效复制,在大脑中可检测到,并且表现出比最近的进化枝 2.3.4.4b(基因型 B3.13 病毒)更低的致死率。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明了感染奶牛的 H5N1 病毒的遗传和表型多样性,并有独立 跨物种溢出 事件和哺乳动物适应 突变 的证据。该研究强调了预测新出现的 H5N1 病毒株的哺乳动物致病性的复杂性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调需要继续对奶牛中的 H5N1 病毒进行 监测 和功能表征,以便为潜在人畜共患 传播 的风险评估和防范提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它只关注单一菌株和小鼠模型,可能无法完全代表人类或牛的感染动态。由于样本量小且缺乏人体临床数据,证据强度中等。

Although the virus encoded the mammalian-adapting PB2-E627K substitution, it exhibited comparatively low lethality in mice, highlighting the complexity of mammalian adaptation and pathogenicity in H5N1 viruses. These findings expand current understanding of the genetic and phenotypic diversity of H5N1 viruses infecting dairy cattle and emphasize the importance of continued surveillance and functional characterization of emerging strains.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 高致病性禽流感 A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒最近从禽类 储存宿主 传播到美国奶牛中,引发了人们对哺乳动物适应和公共卫生风险的担忧。该研究旨在表征从威斯康星州奶牛群中新分离出的 H5N1 病毒,以了解其遗传和表型特性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究从 2025 年 12 月从威斯康星州奶牛群收集的散装牛奶中分离并鉴定了分支 2.3.4.4b、基因型 D1.1 H5N1 病毒(A/奶牛/威斯康星州/25G05743-001/2025)。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过在含胚鸡蛋中盲传代来回收传染性病毒。确定了系统发育关系,并评估了该病毒的哺乳动物适应性取代和对小鼠的致病性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析显示,WI5743-H5N1 与之前报道的内华达州和亚利桑那州奶牛中的 D1.1 病毒不同,表明可能是从当地鸟类来源独立引入的。该病毒编码了适应哺乳动物的 PB2-E627K 取代以及 HA、PB1-F2 和 NS1 中的其他氨基酸差异。在小鼠中,WI5743-H5N1 在呼吸组织中有效复制,在大脑中可检测到,并且表现出比最近的进化枝 2.3.4.4b(基因型 B3.13 病毒)更低的致死率。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明了感染奶牛的 H5N1 病毒的遗传和表型多样性,并有独立 跨物种溢出 事件和哺乳动物适应 突变 的证据。该研究强调了预测新出现的 H5N1 病毒株的哺乳动物致病性的复杂性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调需要继续对奶牛中的 H5N1 病毒进行 监测 和功能表征,以便为潜在人畜共患 传播 的风险评估和防范提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它只关注单一菌株和小鼠模型,可能无法完全代表人类或牛的感染动态。由于样本量小且缺乏人体临床数据,证据强度中等。

papers.title: PEGylated PolyaspartamideNanomicelle Delivery ofSelf-amplifying Avian Influenza mRNA Vaccine
papers.abstract: Abstract The avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a major threat to the poultry industry and public health worldwide, highlighting the need for effective vaccines. Currently, the influenza vaccine for human use is an inactivated vaccine produced from eggs, which requires time-consuming and safe production processes. Messenger RNA (mRNA) is a transcriptional product of cells that can directly produce proteins, with no safety concerns regarding DNA template residues or integrated mutations in the genomic DNA. Recently, COVID-19 vaccines developed using mRNA to express the vaccine antigen have resulted in effective humoral and cellular immune responses. Additionally, mRNA can induce a robust cellular Toll-like receptor immune response and has the potential to serve as a promising vaccine adjuvant. In this study, we developed PEGylated polyamino polyplex nanomicelles encapsulating mRNA that expresses the AIV antigen. These nanomicelles were manufactured as an AIV vaccine, and their efficacy was evaluated in vivo. We produced a highly translation-effective, self-amplifying mRNA (saRNA) that expresses the main antigen, hemagglutinin (HA) protein of AIV. Subsequently, we encapsulated the HA-expressing saRNA in self-assembled polymeric nanomicelles using a PEGylated polyaspartamide block copolymer. Then, we compared the mRNA-loaded nanomicelle administration scenarios and the vaccine-elicited humoral (antibody titer and hemagglutination inhibition capability) and cellular immune responses (interferon-gamma [IFN-γ] and interleukin-4 [IL-4] cytokines) in mice. Our results demonstrated the successful development of an avian mRNA vaccine using polyamino self-assembled nanomicelles, which significantly enhanced both the humoral and cellular immune responses against the AIV antigen, providing a valuable reference for the further improvement of avian influenza mRNA vaccines in the future.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the urgent need for improved avian influenza virus (AIV) vaccines due to the global threat posed by AIV to poultry and public health. It highlights limitations of current inactivated egg-based vaccines and explores mRNA vaccine technology as a promising alternative.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research developed a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine expressing the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of AIV encapsulated in PEGylated polyaspartamide nanomicelles. The vaccine's efficacy was evaluated in vivo by comparing humoral and cellular immune responses in mice.
analysis.methods: A highly translation-effective, self-amplifying mRNA (saRNA) expressing the HA protein of AIV was produced and encapsulated in self-assembled polymeric nanomicelles using a PEGylated polyaspartamide block copolymer. The study compared vaccine-elicited humoral (antibody titer and hemagglutination inhibition capability) and cellular immune responses (IFN-γ and IL-4 cytokines) in mice.
analysis.main_results: The results demonstrated that the avian mRNA vaccine using polyamino self-assembled nanomicelles significantly enhanced both humoral and cellular immune responses against the AIV antigen in mice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that the nanomicelle-encapsulated saRNA vaccine platform effectively induces robust immune responses, suggesting a valuable approach for improving avian influenza mRNA vaccines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the potential of mRNA-based nanomicelle vaccines as a platform for avian influenza prevention, offering a faster and potentially safer alternative to traditional egg-based inactivated vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vivo mouse studies and lacks human clinical data, which constrains generalizability to poultry or human populations. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of broader validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine expressing the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of avian influenza virus (AIV) encapsulated in PEGylated polyaspartamide nanomicelles. The vaccine was evaluated in mice, demonstrating significant enhancement of both humoral and cellular immune responses against AIV. The authors propose this platform as a promising alternative to traditional egg-based inactivated vaccines, citing the rapid production and safety advantages of mRNA technology. However, the evidence is limited to preclinical mouse models and lacks human or poultry validation, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于AIV对家禽和公共卫生构成全球威胁,该研究解决了对改良禽流感病毒(AIV)疫苗的迫切需求。它强调了当前基于灭活鸡蛋的 疫苗 的局限性,并探索 mRNA 疫苗 技术作为一种有前途的替代方案。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了一种自我扩增的 mRNA 疫苗,表达封装在聚乙二醇化聚天冬酰胺纳米胶束中的 AIV 血凝素 (HA) 蛋白。通过比较小鼠体内的体液和细胞 免疫应答 来评估 疫苗 的体内功效。
elements_zh.methods: 使用聚乙二醇化聚天冬酰胺嵌段共聚物,生产了表达 AIV HA 蛋白的高度翻译效率、自扩增 mRNA (saRNA),并将其封装在自组装聚合物纳米胶束中。该研究比较了 疫苗 在小鼠中引发的体液(抗体滴度和血凝抑制能力)和细胞 免疫应答(IFN-γ 和 IL-4 细胞因子)。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,使用聚氨基自组装纳米胶束的禽类 mRNA 疫苗 显着增强了小鼠体内针对 AIV 抗原的体液和细胞 免疫应答。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为纳米胶束封装的 saRNA 疫苗 平台有效诱导强大的 免疫应答 的证据,这表明了一种改善 禽流感 mRNA 疫苗 的有价值的方法。

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The research developed a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine expressing the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of AIV encapsulated in PEGylated polyaspartamide nanomicelles. The vaccine's efficacy was evaluated in vivo by comparing humoral and cellular immune responses in mice.
analysis_en.methods: A highly translation-effective, self-amplifying mRNA (saRNA) expressing the HA protein of AIV was produced and encapsulated in self-assembled polymeric nanomicelles using a PEGylated polyaspartamide block copolymer. papers.title_zh: 聚乙二醇化聚天冬酰胺纳米胶束递送自扩增 禽流感 mRNA 疫苗
papers.source_body_en: Abstract The avian influenza virus (AIV) poses a major threat to the poultry industry and public health worldwide, highlighting the need for effective vaccines. Currently, the influenza vaccine for human use is an inactivated vaccine produced from eggs, which requires time-consuming and safe production processes. Messenger RNA (mRNA) is a transcriptional product of cells that can directly produce proteins, with no safety concerns regarding DNA template residues or integrated mutations in the genomic DNA. Recently, COVID-19 vaccines developed using mRNA to express the vaccine antigen have resulted in effective humoral and cellular immune responses. Additionally, mRNA can induce a robust cellular Toll-like receptor immune response and has the potential to serve as a promising vaccine adjuvant. In this study, we developed PEGylated polyamino polyplex nanomicelles encapsulating mRNA that expresses the AIV antigen. These nanomicelles were manufactured as an AIV vaccine, and their efficacy was evaluated in vivo. We produced a highly translation-effective, self-amplifying mRNA (saRNA) that expresses the main antigen, hemagglutinin (HA) protein of AIV. Subsequently, we encapsulated the HA-expressing saRNA in self-assembled polymeric nanomicelles using a PEGylated polyaspartamide block copolymer. Then, we compared the mRNA-loaded nanomicelle administration scenarios and the vaccine-elicited humoral (antibody titer and hemagglutination inhibition capability) and cellular immune responses (interferon-gamma [IFN-γ] and interleukin-4 [IL-4] cytokines) in mice. Our results demonstrated the successful development of an avian mRNA vaccine using polyamino self-assembled nanomicelles, which significantly enhanced both the humoral and cellular immune responses against the AIV antigen, providing a valuable reference for the further improvement of avian influenza mRNA vaccines in the future.

papers.full_text: The arrival of the highly pathogenic H5N1 strain of bird flu in Aotearoa New Zealand last month triggered a national response years in the making. By then, surveillance systems, species protection plans and even vaccines for some birds were already in place as part of a coordinated approach led by the Ministry for Primary Industries. Yet even these preparations may not be enough to save some of the country’s rarest birds. Many survive in tiny, isolated populations with limited genetic diversity. For these highly vulnerable species, the outcome may depend not only on conservation efforts, but also on chance. Genetic diversity acts as nature’s insurance policy against disease. In large populations, some individuals are more likely to survive an outbreak and help the population recover. But in small, isolated populations with little genetic diversity, those odds are much lower, leaving species far more vulnerable to extinction. Why vaccines can only do so much H5N1 has caused mass mortality events in wild birds around the world since emerging in 2020, making it one of the most significant disease threats many species have faced in decades. Vaccines offer one important layer of protection, but they are no silver bullet. A Department of Conservation-led vaccine trial involving five intensively managed threatened species found that effective protection requires at least two doses administered a few weeks apart. In kakī – the critically endangered black stilt and one of the world’s rarest wading birds – immunity declined after three months, meaning a third dose will be needed. With the trial now complete and H5N1 in New Zealand, vaccinations are underway, beginning with 300 individuals from the five species involved in the study. The greater challenge, however, is delivering that protection in the wild. Catching a threatened bird once can be difficult. Catching the same bird again, at exactly the right time for a second or third dose, can be harder still. Vaccinate too early and immunity may wane before the virus arrives. Vaccinate too late and the opportunity may be missed. These practical constraints mean conservation teams cannot simply vaccinate every bird. Instead, they must make difficult decisions about where limited time and resources will have the greatest impact. On Rēkohu/Wharekauri/Chatham Islands, for example, plans are underway to vaccinate several of its threatened species, including black robin (karure, kakaruia). The species’ small population on Maung’ Rē/Mangere may make it possible to vaccinate every individual with two doses. On nearby Hokoreoreoro/Rangatira, however, the larger population is likely to require a different approach, with efforts focused on vaccinating as many birds as can be reliably caught and recaptured while balancing the needs of other species. The harsh reality is that some birds will receive the right protection at the right time, but others will not. Different birds, different risks Just as importantly, not all species face the same level of risk from H5N1. It varies depending on where those species live and how they behave. For colonial nesting species such as many seabirds, breeding creates the ideal conditions for the virus to spread, as birds gather closely in large numbers. For solitary nesters such as kakī, however, breeding is one of the safer times of year because individuals are more widely dispersed. Their risk increases outside the breeding season, when they congregate at estuaries alongside other bird species. If bird flu does push some species even closer to extinction, it will not be for lack of effort. Across the country, dedicated teams will be working tirelessly to protect the country’s most vulnerable wildlife. To date, the incursion remains limited. Two wild birds in the Wellington region have tested positive for H5N1, with no further detections since mid-July and no evidence of widespread mortality in wildlife or spread into poultry. But overseas experience has shown how quickly the situation can change, making continued surveillance and preparedness essential. Recent media coverage of an injured ruru (morepork) offered a glimpse of how difficult and emotional those decisions can be. In the months and years ahead, conservation staff will need not only the best available science, but also patience, understanding and kindness from the communities they serve. For now, H5N1 is the immediate threat. It is unlikely to be the last. As emerging diseases become an increasingly important conservation challenge, building resilient species and ecosystems will be just as important as responding to each new outbreak. If you find a single sick, injured or dead native bird, contact the Department of Conservation (0800 362 468). If you find three or more sick or dead birds together, report it immediately to the Ministry for Primary Industries (0800 80 99 66).

papers.title_original: NZ has spent years preparing for H5N1 bird flu. For some species, it may not be enough

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study examines why New Zealand’s existing H5N1 preparedness may be insufficient for its most vulnerable bird species despite years of national planning and surveillance systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The analysis synthesizes national surveillance systems, conservation plans, and vaccine trials led by the Ministry for Primary Industries and Department of Conservation, focusing on threatened bird species with limited genetic diversity.
analysis.methods: The paper reviews vaccine trial protocols for five intensively managed threatened species, including dosing schedules and immunity duration, and evaluates practical constraints in delivering multi-dose vaccination in wild populations.
analysis.main_results: Vaccine effectiveness requires at least two doses, with immunity declining after three months in kakī, necessitating a third dose. Practical challenges include the difficulty of recapturing birds for subsequent doses and balancing limited resources across species and locations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors highlight that while vaccines provide critical protection, their real-world application is constrained by logistical challenges and species-specific risks, underscoring the need for targeted conservation strategies rather than blanket vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize prioritizing vaccination efforts for species with feasible recapture rates and focusing on high-risk periods, such as colonial nesting seasons, to mitigate H5N1 impacts on New Zealand’s rarest birds.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is observational and based on a single vaccine trial with five species, lacking broader population-level data or randomized comparisons, which limits generalizability and strength of inference.

analysis.summary_en: New Zealand’s H5N1 preparedness includes surveillance systems, species protection plans, and vaccines for some birds, yet these measures may not suffice for its most vulnerable species. Small, isolated populations with limited genetic diversity face heightened extinction risk, as immunity from vaccines wanes without repeated doses. A Department of Conservation-led trial found that effective protection requires at least two doses, with kakī needing a third dose after three months due to declining immunity. Practical constraints, such as the difficulty of recapturing birds for subsequent doses, further complicate vaccination efforts. Conservation teams must prioritize species and locations where vaccination is feasible, such as the black robin on Maung’ Rē/Mangere, while balancing resources across other threatened species. Risk varies by species behavior, with colonial nesters facing higher transmission risks during breeding seasons. While H5N1 detections remain limited in New Zealand, overseas experience underscores the need for continued surveillance and adaptive conservation strategies.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study examines why New Zealand’s existing H5N1 preparedness may be insufficient for its most vulnerable bird species despite years of national planning and surveillance systems.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The analysis synthesizes national surveillance systems, conservation plans, and vaccine trials led by the Ministry for Primary Industries and Department of Conservation, focusing on threatened bird species with limited genetic diversity.
analysis_en.methods: The paper reviews vaccine trial protocols for five intensively managed threatened species, including dosing schedules and immunity duration, and evaluates practical constraints in delivering multi-dose vaccination in wild populations.
analysis_en.main_results: Vaccine effectiveness requires at least two doses, with immunity declining after three months in kakī, necessitating a third dose. Practical challenges include the difficulty of recapturing birds for subsequent doses and balancing limited resources across species and locations.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors highlight that while vaccines provide critical protection, their real-world application is constrained by logistical challenges and species-specific risks, underscoring the need for targeted conservation strategies rather than blanket vaccination.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize prioritizing vaccination efforts for species with feasible recapture rates and focusing on high-risk periods, such as colonial nesting seasons, to mitigate H5N1 impacts on New Zealand’s rarest birds.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is observational and based on a single vaccine trial with five species, lacking broader population-level data or randomized comparisons, which limits generalizability and strength of inference.

Liz Brown, CC BY-NC-ND NZ has spent years preparing for H5N1 bird flu. For some species, it may not be enough Published: August 17, 2026 3:17pm EDT The arrival of the highly pathogenic H5N1 strain of bird flu in Aotearoa New Zealand last month triggered a national response years in the making. By then, surveillance systems, species protection plans and even vaccines for some birds were already in place as part of a coordinated approach led by the Ministry for Primary Industries. Yet even these preparations may not be enough to save some of the country’s rarest birds. Many survive in tiny, isolated populations with limited genetic diversity. For these highly vulnerable species, the outcome may depend not only on conservation efforts, but also on chance. Genetic diversity acts as nature’s insurance policy against disease. In large populations, some individuals are more likely to survive an outbreak and help the population recover. But in small, isolated populations with little genetic diversity, those odds are much lower, leaving species far more vulnerable to extinction. Why vaccines can only do so much H5N1 has caused mass mortality events in wild birds around the world since emerging in 2020, making it one of the most significant disease threats many species have faced in decades. Vaccines offer one important layer of protection, but they are no silver bullet. A Department of Conservation-led vaccine trial involving five intensively managed threatened species found that effective protection requires at least two doses administered a few weeks apart. In kakī – the critically endangered black stilt and one of the world’s rarest wading birds – immunity declined after three months, meaning a third dose will be needed. With the trial now complete and H5N1 in New Zealand, vaccinations are underway, beginning with 300 individuals from the five species involved in the study. The greater challenge, however, is delivering that protection in the wild. Catching a threatened bird once can be difficult. Catching the same bird again, at exactly the right time for a second or third dose, can be harder still. Vaccinate too early and immunity may wane before the virus arrives. Vaccinate too late and the opportunity may be missed. These practical constraints mean conservation teams cannot simply vaccinate every bird. Instead, they must make difficult decisions about where limited time and resources will have the greatest impact. On Rēkohu/Wharekauri/Chatham Islands, for example, plans are underway to vaccinate several of its threatened species, including black robin (karure, kakaruia). The black robin (karure, kakaruia) endemic to the Chatham Islands, lying to the east of New Zealand. Robin Bush/Getty Images The species’ small population on Maung’ Rē/Mangere may make it possible to vaccinate every individual with two doses. On nearby Hokoreoreoro/Rangatira, however, the larger population is likely to require a different approach, with efforts focused on vaccinating as many birds as can be reliably caught and recaptured while balancing the needs of other species. The harsh reality is that some birds will receive the right protection at the right time, but others will not. Different birds, different risks Just as importantly, not all species face the same level of risk from H5N1. It varies depending on where those species live and how they behave. For colonial nesting species such as many seabirds, breeding creates the ideal conditions for the virus to spread, as birds gather closely in large numbers. For solitary nesters such as kakī, however, breeding is one of the safer times of year because individuals are more widely dispersed. Their risk increases outside the breeding season, when they congregate at estuaries alongside other bird species. If bird flu does push some species even closer to extinction, it will not be for lack of effort. Across the country, dedicated teams will be working tirelessly to protect the country’s most vulnerable wildlife. To date, the incursion remains limited. Two wild birds in the Wellington region have tested positive for H5N1, with no further detections since mid-July and no evidence of widespread mortality in wildlife or spread into poultry. But overseas experience has shown how quickly the situation can change, making continued surveillance and preparedness essential. Recent media coverage of an injured ruru (morepork) offered a glimpse of how difficult and emotional those decisions can be. In the months and years ahead, conservation staff will need not only the best available science, but also patience, understanding and kindness from the communities they serve. For now, H5N1 is the immediate threat. It is unlikely to be the last. As emerging diseases become an increasingly important conservation challenge, building resilient species and ecosystems will be just as important as responding to each new outbreak. If you find a single sick, injured or dead native bird, contact the Department of Conservation (0800 362 468). If you find three or more sick or dead birds together, report it immediately to the Ministry for Primary Industries (0800 80 99 66). papers.title: Serovigilancia de influenza aviar H5N2 en patos y gansos domésticos de Río Blanco, San Marcos, Guatemala
papers.abstract: Serological monitoring was conducted in domestic ducks and geese from the municipality of Río Blanco, San Marcos, in Guatemala’s western highlands. A total of 112 serum samples were taken from 83 Muscovy ducks (Cairina moschata) and 29 domestic geese (Anser anser var. domesticus) to determine the seroprevalence of H5N2 Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI), by the haemagglutination inhibition test. A point seroprevalence of 0.89% was determined, with only 1 Muscovy duck out of 112 showing antibodies considered positive for the disease. The results indicate the presence of antibodies against H5N2 LPAI in a duck not vaccinated by the animal health service, suggesting exposure to the virus and possible circulation in the area. Therefore, it is necessary to remove obstacles to implement adequate surveillance and control strategies in the country.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A serological survey was conducted in Río Blanco, San Marcos, Guatemala, from which 112 serum samples were collected from 83 Muscovy ducks (Cairina moschata) and 29 domestic geese (Anser anser var.
analysis.methods: Seroprevalence of H5N2 LPAI was determined using the haemagglutination inhibition test on serum samples collected from the specified domestic bird populations.
analysis.main_results: The point seroprevalence of H5N2 LPAI was found to be 0.89%, with only one Muscovy duck out of 112 showing positive antibodies for the virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The presence of antibodies in a non-vaccinated duck suggests possible exposure to the virus and indicates the potential circulation of H5N2 LPAI in the area, which is a novel finding for this region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the need for enhanced surveillance and control strategies to manage the potential spread of H5N2 LPAI in domestic bird populations, which could have implications for public health and animal welfare.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted serological monitoring to assess the prevalence of H5N2 Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI) in domestic ducks and geese in Río Blanco, San Marcos, Guatemala. A total of 112 serum samples were collected from 83 Muscovy ducks and 29 domestic geese, and the haemagglutination inhibition test was used to determine seroprevalence. The results showed a point seroprevalence of 0.89%, with only one Muscovy duck testing positive for antibodies against H5N2 LPAI. This suggests possible exposure and circulation of the virus in the area, which is a novel finding. The study highlights the importance of implementing adequate surveillance and control strategies to manage the potential spread of H5N2 LPAI. However, the study is limited by its focus on a single municipality and the use of a single serological test, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估危地马拉圣马科斯里奥布兰科家鸭和鹅中 H5N2 低致病性 血清流行率 (LPAI) 的 血清流行率,以了解其潜在传播和对鸟类种群的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在危地马拉圣马科斯的里奥布兰科进行了血清学调查,从83只番鸭(Cairina moschata)和29只家鹅(Anser anser var.)采集了112份血清样本。
elements_zh.methods: H5N2 LPAI 的 血清流行率 是通过对从特定家禽种群采集的血清样品进行血凝抑制试验来测定的。
elements_zh.main_results: H5N2 LPAI 的 血清流行率 点为 0.89%,112 只番鸭中只有 1 只表现出病毒抗体阳性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 未接种疫苗的鸭子体内出现抗体表明可能接触过该病毒,并表明该地区可能存在 H5N2 LPAI 传播,这是该地区的一项新发现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调需要加强 监测 和控制策略来管理 H5N2 LPAI 在家禽种群中的潜在传播,这可能对公共卫生和动物福利产生影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它只关注单个城市并使用单一血清学检测,可能无法完全掌握 H5N2 LPAI 的传播范围。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

A total of 112 serum samples were taken from 83 Muscovy ducks (Cairina moschata) and 29 domestic geese (Anser anser var. domesticus) to determine the seroprevalence of H5N2 Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI), by the haemagglutination inhibition test. A point seroprevalence of 0.89% was determined, with only 1 Muscovy duck out of 112 showing antibodies considered positive for the disease. The results indicate the presence of antibodies against H5N2 LPAI in a duck not vaccinated by the animal health service, suggesting exposure to the virus and possible circulation in the area. Therefore, it is necessary to remove obstacles to implement adequate surveillance and control strategies in the country.

papers.title: Host cell entry receptors as pharmacological targets in respiratory viral infections: from biology to clinical translation
papers.abstract: Respiratory viral infections caused by seasonal influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and pandemic-potential coronaviruses are responsible for several million hospitalisations and an estimated several hundred thousand deaths each year, a burden underscored by the severe 2024–2025 influenza season and the continued emergence of zoonotic threats such as clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1. This review critically examines the pharmacological basis for targeting host cell-surface receptors as a strategy for the treatment and prophylaxis of respiratory viral infections, evaluates the current evidence for each major receptor axis, and identifies the key translational gaps that must be addressed. Respiratory viruses, including influenza, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV, collectively cause millions of hospitalisations annually, and the persistent challenges of antigenic drift, zoonotic emergence, and antiviral resistance highlight the need for mechanistically distinct strategies. Host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors (ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, TMPRSS2) exploit genetically stable host factors required for viral entry. Across the receptor axes reviewed here, we appraise more than a dozen candidate agents spanning preclinical development through Phase III evaluation, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 and receptor-blocking monoclonal antibodies, the sialidase fusion protein DAS181, and avian IgY preparations. This evidence reveals a consistent gap between robust preclinical activity and as-yet-limited clinical efficacy. We conclude that host receptor targeting is a mechanistically rational but still clinically unproven component of the respiratory antiviral landscape; its value is most plausibly realised in defined niches—prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination with direct-acting antivirals—and within pandemic preparedness frameworks, provided that the safety, delivery, and trial-design challenges identified here are resolved.

papers.title_original: Host cell entry receptors as pharmacological targets in respiratory viral infections: from biology to clinical translation

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines pharmacological targeting of host cell-surface receptors as a strategy for treating and preventing respiratory viral infections, focusing on avian influenza A viruses (e.g., H5N1, H5N6, H7N9) and other zoonotic respiratory pathogens. The central question addresses the translational potential of host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors such as ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, and TMPRSS2 for avian influenza and related zoonotic threats.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that critically evaluates the pharmacological basis for targeting host cell receptors in respiratory viral infections, appraising candidate agents across preclinical and clinical stages. It identifies translational gaps but does not report systematic search dates, eligibility criteria, or included-study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that host receptor targeting is mechanistically rational but remains clinically unproven for respiratory viral infections. It highlights a consistent gap between robust preclinical activity and limited clinical efficacy across receptor axes, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 antibodies, and sialidase fusion proteins.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies unresolved challenges in translating preclinical efficacy to clinical outcomes, including safety concerns, delivery barriers, and trial-design limitations. It notes that while HDTs target conserved host factors, their clinical value remains unproven, particularly in pandemic preparedness frameworks.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes resolving safety, delivery, and trial-design challenges to realize the potential of host receptor targeting in prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination with direct-acting antivirals. It emphasizes the need for pandemic preparedness frameworks to integrate HDTs, contingent on addressing identified translational gaps.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates host cell receptor targeting as a strategy for treating and preventing respiratory viral infections, with a focus on avian influenza A viruses and zoonotic threats. It synthesizes evidence on host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors such as ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, and TMPRSS2, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 antibodies, and sialidase fusion proteins. The review concludes that while HDTs are mechanistically rational, their clinical efficacy remains unproven, with a consistent gap between preclinical promise and limited real-world success. Key challenges include safety, delivery barriers, and trial-design limitations. The authors prioritize addressing these translational gaps to enable HDTs in prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination therapies, particularly within pandemic preparedness frameworks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了 宿主 细胞表面受体的药理学靶向作为治疗和预防呼吸道病毒感染的策略,重点关注 禽流感 A 病毒(例如 H5N1、H5N6、H7N9)和其他人畜共患呼吸道病原体。核心问题涉及针对 宿主 和相关人畜共患威胁的保守受体(如 ACE2、DPP4、唾液酸和 TMPRSS2)的 宿主 定向疗法 (HDT) 的转化潜力。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性综合文章,批判性地评估了针对呼吸道病毒感染中 宿主 细胞受体的药理学基础,评估了临床前和临床阶段的候选药物。它确定了翻译差距,但不报告系统检索日期、资格标准或纳入研究计数。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,宿主 受体靶向在机制上是合理的,但在呼吸道病毒感染方面尚未得到临床证实。它强调了跨受体轴(包括 TMPRSS2 抑制剂、可溶性 ACE2 诱饵、抗 CD147 抗体和唾液酸酶融合蛋白)的强大临床前活性和有限的临床疗效之间的一致差距。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了将临床前疗效转化为临床结果方面尚未解决的挑战,包括安全性问题、交付障碍和试验设计限制。它指出,虽然 HDT 以保守的 宿主 因子为目标,但其临床价值尚未得到证实,特别是在大流行防范框架中。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查优先考虑解决安全性、交付和试验设计挑战,以实现 宿主 受体靶向在预防、早期门诊 治疗 以及与直接作用 抗病毒药物 组合方面的潜力。它强调大流行病防范框架需要整合 HDT,这取决于解决已确定的转化差距。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines pharmacological targeting of host cell-surface receptors as a strategy for treating and preventing respiratory viral infections, focusing on avian influenza A viruses (e.g., H5N1, H5N6, H7N9) and other zoonotic respiratory pathogens. The central question addresses the translational potential of host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors such as ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, and TMPRSS2 for avian influenza and related zoonotic threats.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that critically evaluates the pharmacological basis for targeting host cell receptors in respiratory viral infections, appraising candidate agents across preclinical and clinical stages. It identifies translational gaps but does not report systematic search dates, eligibility criteria, or included-study counts.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that host receptor targeting is mechanistically rational but remains clinically unproven for respiratory viral infections. It highlights a consistent gap between robust preclinical activity and limited clinical efficacy across receptor axes, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 antibodies, and sialidase fusion proteins.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies unresolved challenges in translating preclinical efficacy to clinical outcomes, including safety concerns, delivery barriers, and trial-design limitations. It notes that while HDTs target conserved host factors, their clinical value remains unproven, particularly in pandemic preparedness frameworks.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes resolving safety, delivery, and trial-design challenges to realize the potential of host receptor targeting in prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination with direct-acting antivirals. It emphasizes the need for pandemic preparedness frameworks to integrate HDTs, contingent on addressing identified translational gaps.

papers.title_zh: 宿主 细胞进入受体作为呼吸道病毒感染的药理学靶点:从生物学到临床转化
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory viral infections caused by seasonal influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and pandemic-potential coronaviruses are responsible for several million hospitalisations and an estimated several hundred thousand deaths each year, a burden underscored by the severe 2024–2025 influenza season and the continued emergence of zoonotic threats such as clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1. This review critically examines the pharmacological basis for targeting host cell-surface receptors as a strategy for the treatment and prophylaxis of respiratory viral infections, evaluates the current evidence for each major receptor axis, and identifies the key translational gaps that must be addressed. Respiratory viruses, including influenza, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV, collectively cause millions of hospitalisations annually, and the persistent challenges of antigenic drift, zoonotic emergence, and antiviral resistance highlight the need for mechanistically distinct strategies. Host-directed therapies (HDTs) targeting conserved receptors (ACE2, DPP4, sialic acids, TMPRSS2) exploit genetically stable host factors required for viral entry. Across the receptor axes reviewed here, we appraise more than a dozen candidate agents spanning preclinical development through Phase III evaluation, including TMPRSS2 inhibitors, soluble ACE2 decoys, anti-CD147 and receptor-blocking monoclonal antibodies, the sialidase fusion protein DAS181, and avian IgY preparations. This evidence reveals a consistent gap between robust preclinical activity and as-yet-limited clinical efficacy. We conclude that host receptor targeting is a mechanistically rational but still clinically unproven component of the respiratory antiviral landscape; its value is most plausibly realised in defined niches—prophylaxis, early outpatient treatment, and combination with direct-acting antivirals—and within pandemic preparedness frameworks, provided that the safety, delivery, and trial-design challenges identified here are resolved.
papers.abstract_zh: 由季节性流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和潜在大流行的冠状病毒引起的呼吸道病毒感染每年导致数百万人住院,估计有数十万人死亡,2024-2025 年严重的流感季节和人畜共患威胁(如进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5N1)的持续出现加剧了这一负担。本综述批判性地研究了靶向 宿主 细胞表面受体作为 治疗 和预防呼吸道病毒感染的策略的药理学基础,评估了每个主要受体轴的当前证据,并确定了必须解决的关键翻译差距。呼吸道病毒,包括流感、RSV、SARS-CoV-2 和 MERS-CoV,每年总共导致数百万人住院,抗原漂移、人畜共患疾病的出现和 抗病毒药物 耐药性等持续挑战突出表明需要采取机制上不同的策略。针对保守受体(ACE2、DPP4、唾液酸、TMPRSS2)的 宿主 定向疗法 (HDT) 利用病毒进入所需的遗传稳定的 宿主 因子。在此回顾的受体轴中,我们评估了十多种从临床前开发到 III 期评估的候选药物,包括 TMPRSS2 抑制剂、可溶性 ACE2 诱饵、抗 CD147 和受体阻断单克隆抗体、唾液酸酶融合蛋白 DAS181 和禽类 IgY 制剂。这一证据揭示了强大的临床前活性与迄今为止有限的临床疗效之间的一致差距。我们得出的结论是,宿主 受体靶向是呼吸 抗病毒药物 景观中机械合理但尚未得到临床证实的组成部分;它的价值最有可能在特定的领域(预防、早期门诊 治疗 以及与直接作用的 抗病毒药物 组合)以及大流行防范框架内实现,前提是此处确定的安全性、交付和试验设计挑战得到解决。

papers.title: Conserved influenza A epitope candidate regions and a benchmark of ESM-2 sequence features
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus antigenic drift forces annual vaccine reformulation, motivating the search for conserved epitope candidates that could support broadly protective vaccines. We systematically screened influenza A virus sequences (H1N1, H3N2, H5N1; nine viral proteins) to define 98 conserved candidate regions, 38 of which were identical across the H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1 consensus sequences, all in the polymerase complex and nucleoprotein (PB2, PB1, PA, NP), whereas the ten surface-glycoprotein (HA/NA) candidates were subtype-specific. We then benchmarked two protein-language-model (ESM-2) features against alignment conservation. Group-masked log-probability correlated moderately with MSA conservation (Spearman rho = 0.25 to 0.39 for HA) but provided no incremental value for T-cell epitope discrimination (change in AUROC +0.004, p = 0.46); attention-derived contact-density was not a valid solvent-accessibility proxy. A curated antibody-epitope benchmark (22 clusters, 5 neutralization-supported) was underpowered for a high-confidence B-cell test. We document data-quality and reproducibility pitfalls (length heterogeneity, coordinate mapping, and pseudoreplication) and release the auditable benchmark. These results provide an auditable candidate resource and show that, in the evaluated benchmarks, ESM-2 sequence scores did not improve epitope prioritization beyond alignment-derived conservation.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及对多种亚型和蛋白质的甲型流感病毒序列进行系统筛选,重点关注聚合酶复合物和核蛋白内的保守区域。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用群体屏蔽对数概率和注意力衍生接触密度作为指标,对 ESM-2 序列特征与比对保守进行基准测试。
elements_zh.main_results: 组屏蔽对数概率与 MSA 保守性显示出中等相关性,但没有改善 T 细胞表位辨别力,而注意力衍生的接触密度并不是有效的溶剂可及性代理。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在评估的基准中,ESM-2 序列评分并未增强表位优先级,超越传统的比对衍生保护方法。

papers.title_zh: 保守的甲型流感表位候选区域和 ESM-2 序列特征的基准
papers.source_body_en: Influenza A virus antigenic drift forces annual vaccine reformulation, motivating the search for conserved epitope candidates that could support broadly protective vaccines. We systematically screened influenza A virus sequences (H1N1, H3N2, H5N1; nine viral proteins) to define 98 conserved candidate regions, 38 of which were identical across the H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1 consensus sequences, all in the polymerase complex and nucleoprotein (PB2, PB1, PA, NP), whereas the ten surface-glycoprotein (HA/NA) candidates were subtype-specific. We then benchmarked two protein-language-model (ESM-2) features against alignment conservation. Group-masked log-probability correlated moderately with MSA conservation (Spearman rho = 0.25 to 0.39 for HA) but provided no incremental value for T-cell epitope discrimination (change in AUROC +0.004, p = 0.46); attention-derived contact-density was not a valid solvent-accessibility proxy. A curated antibody-epitope benchmark (22 clusters, 5 neutralization-supported) was underpowered for a high-confidence B-cell test. We document data-quality and reproducibility pitfalls (length heterogeneity, coordinate mapping, and pseudoreplication) and release the auditable benchmark. These results provide an auditable candidate resource and show that, in the evaluated benchmarks, ESM-2 sequence scores did not improve epitope prioritization beyond alignment-derived conservation.
papers.abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒抗原漂移迫使每年重新配制 疫苗,从而激发了对可支持广泛保护性 疫苗 的保守候选表位的搜索。我们系统地筛选了甲型流感病毒序列(H1N1、H3N2、H5N1;九种病毒蛋白),以确定 98 个保守候选区域,其中 38 个在 H1N1、H3N2 和 H5N1 共有序列中是相同的,全部位于聚合酶复合物和核蛋白(PB2、PB1、PA、NP)中,而 10 个表面糖蛋白(HA/NA)候选区域是亚型特异性的。然后,我们对两个蛋白质语言模型 (ESM-2) 特征与对齐保守性进行了基准测试。组屏蔽对数概率与 MSA 保守性适度相关(对于 HA,Spearman rho = 0.25 至 0.39),但没有为 T 细胞表位辨别提供增量值(AUROC 变化 +0.004,p = 0.46);注意力衍生的接触密度并不是有效的溶剂可及性代理。精心设计的抗体表位基准(22 个簇,5 个支持中和)对于高置信度 B 细胞测试来说动力不足。我们记录数据质量和可重复性缺陷(长度异质性、坐标映射和伪复制)并发布可审核的基准。这些结果提供了可审核的候选资源,并表明,在评估的基准中,ESM-2 序列评分并没有改善除比对衍生的保护之外的表位优先顺序。
papers.summary_zh: 甲型流感病毒抗原漂移迫使每年重新配制 疫苗,从而激发了对可支持广泛保护性 疫苗 的保守候选表位的搜索。我们系统地筛选了甲型流感病毒序列(H1N1、H3N2、H5N1;九种病毒蛋白),以确定 98 个保守候选区域,其中 38 个在 H1N1、H3N2 和 H5N1 共有序列中是相同的,全部位于聚合酶复合物和核蛋白(PB2、PB1、PA、NP)中,而 10 个表面糖蛋白(HA/NA)候选区域是亚型特异性的。然后,我们对两个蛋白质语言模型 (ESM-2) 特征与对齐保守性进行了基准测试。组屏蔽对数概率与 MSA 保守性适度相关(对于 HA,Spearman rho = 0.25 至 0.39),但没有为 T 细胞表位辨别提供增量值(AUROC 变化 +0.004,p = 0.46);注意力衍生的接触密度并不是有效的溶剂可及性代理。精心设计的抗体表位基准(22 个簇,5 个支持中和)对于高置信度 B 细胞测试来说动力不足。我们记录数据质量和可重复性缺陷(长度异质性、坐标映射和伪复制)并发布可审核的基准。这些结果提供了可审核的候选资源,并表明,在评估的基准中,ESM-2 序列评分并没有改善除比对衍生的保护之外的表位优先顺序。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在鉴定甲型流感病毒中的保守候选表位,以支持广泛保护性 疫苗 的开发,因为抗原漂移需要每年重新配制 疫苗。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及对多种亚型和蛋白质的甲型流感病毒序列进行系统筛选,重点关注聚合酶复合物和核蛋白内的保守区域。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用群体屏蔽对数概率和注意力衍生接触密度作为指标,对 ESM-2 序列特征与比对保守进行基准测试。
analysis_zh.main_results: 组屏蔽对数概率与 MSA 保守性显示出中等相关性,但没有改善 T 细胞表位辨别力,而注意力衍生的接触密度并不是有效的溶剂可及性代理。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在评估的基准中,ESM-2 序列评分并未增强表位优先级,超越传统的比对衍生保护方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果为候选表位提供了可审核的资源,并强调了使用 ESM-2 特征对甲型流感病毒进行表位优先排序的局限性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究指出了数据质量和重现性问题,例如长度异质性和假复制,并承认抗体表位基准对于高置信度 B 细胞测试来说动力不足。

Login In Now Don't show this again AseanPlus News Over 1,000 birds found dead in suspected H5N1 outbreak in South Australia Thursday, 20 Aug 2026 | 9:26 PM MYT share bookmark Related Stories Cricket 15h ago Cricket-Australia look for response to 'Darwin Disaster' in second Bangladesh test Technology 12h ago Australia passes law to levy tech giants that fail to pay for local news Japan 1d ago Japan to test hypersonic missiles in Australia under new deal CANBERRA: (Bernama-Xinhua) Authorities in South Australia (SA) said on Thursday (Aug 20) that more than 1,000 birds had died in three separate suspected H5N1 avian influenza mass mortality events on islands off the state's coast, reported Xinhua. South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas told the state parliament that the flocks of crested terns were found dead by surveillance teams on remote offshore islands on Wednesday. He said the deaths represented a significant escalation of bird flu in the state. "The loss of more than 1,000 birds is deeply concerning, and the state government is treating these events with the utmost seriousness,” Malinauskas said. SA is the centre of Australia's H5N1 outbreak, with 177 confirmed cases of H5 bird flu recorded as of Thursday, according to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. In addition to the mass mortality events, Malinauskas said on Thursday that authorities were particularly concerned about a suspected case involving a little penguin found on Kangaroo Island. A survey conducted in October 2025 estimated 704 adult were breeding little penguins on the island, up from 530 in 2024. Malinauskas said authorities would take every practical and appropriate action to protect the state's wildlife and were considering targeted vaccination of captive or managed populations of vulnerable native birds. - Bernama-Xinhua Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for breaking news alerts and key updates! Featured News News #national: Bird Flu Defence Boost: New Grant Backs Poultry Farmers Facing H5N1 The Government is stepping up support for New Zealand’s poultry industry as farmers prepare for the growing threat posed by H5N1 bird flu. A new grant has been launched to help poultry operators strengthen their biosecurity and prepare their farms for the long-term management of highly pathogenic avian influenza. The move comes after H5N1 was... Matthew Tukaki 0 6 Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Threads Share on Telegram The Government is stepping up support for New Zealand’s poultry industry as farmers prepare for the growing threat posed by H5N1 bird flu. A new grant has been launched to help poultry operators strengthen their biosecurity and prepare their farms for the long-term management of highly pathogenic avian influenza. The move comes after H5N1 was detected in New Zealand for the first time in July, when the globally circulating strain was confirmed in a brown skua found at Petone Beach in Wellington. There was no evidence at the time of transmission into commercial poultry. The arrival of H5N1 has changed the country’s approach from preparing for whether the virus will arrive to preparing for the possibility it becomes established among wild birds. Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard has already announced new regulations requiring poultry operations with more than 100 birds to develop, register and implement farm biosecurity plans covering avian disease. Those plans will need to address how farms prevent infection and what happens if disease is detected, including arrangements for humane culling, disposal, cleaning and disinfection. Operators will also face record-keeping and auditing requirements. The Government expects the regulations to come into force by the end of 2026. The poultry sector is particularly important to New Zealand’s food supply and economy. The industry generates an estimated $2.2 billion domestically each year and around $200 million in export revenue. That makes preventing major outbreaks important not only for farmers but also for consumers, food security and trade. The Government and poultry industry already have a formal agreement setting out how they will jointly prepare for and respond to serious exotic poultry diseases. Under that arrangement, the industry contributes 45 percent of general poultry disease readiness and response costs. For an H5N1 response, the industry contribution is 40 percent, with the Government meeting the remaining share of agreed response costs. The potential financial consequences are substantial. An earlier avian influenza outbreak at a commercial egg farm in Otago cost an estimated $25 million, despite being contained to a single property. That outbreak involved a different strain from the H5N1 virus now detected in New Zealand. The new support comes as farmers face the prospect of investing more heavily in farm infrastructure and disease prevention while maintaining the supply of chicken and eggs to New Zealand households. The challenge is particularly significant for smaller poultry operations, which may have fewer resources available to make rapid biosecurity improvements. For the Government, the objective is to strengthen those defences before H5N1 becomes widespread among wild birds and creates a constant infection risk for domestic poultry. With bird flu now inside New Zealand’s borders, biosecurity is no longer simply about keeping the disease out. The focus is increasingly on ensuring farmers, food producers and communities are prepared to live with the risk while protecting flocks, livelihoods and one of the country’s most important sources of affordable protein. #BirdFlu #H5N1 #AvianInfluenza #PoultryNZ #PoultryIndustry #ChickenNZ #EggsNZ #Biosecurity #BiosecurityNZ #AndrewHoggard #MPI #PrimaryIndustries #Farmers #MaoriFarmers #MaoriAgribusiness #WhenuaMaori #FoodSecurity #KaiSecurity #AffordableKai #FoodPrices #FoodSupply #AgricultureNZ #FarmingNZ #RuralNZ #AnimalHealth #FarmBiosecurity #PoultryFarmers #NewZealandFarming #NZEconomy #Aotearoa #MaoriNews #RuralNews #NZNews #NewZealandNews #WaateaNews #RadioWaatea #WaateaDigital Author Matthew Tukaki Share with / Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Threads Share on Pinterest 0 / Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Threads Share on Telegram 0% More posts. Matthew Tukaki 0 6 Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Threads Share on Telegram The Government is stepping up support for New Zealand’s poultry industry as farmers prepare for the growing threat posed by H5N1 bird flu. A new grant has been launched to help poultry operators strengthen their biosecurity and prepare their farms for the long-term management of highly pathogenic avian influenza. The move comes after H5N1 was detected in New Zealand for the first time in July, when the globally circulating strain was confirmed in a brown skua found at Petone Beach in Wellington. There was no evidence at the time of transmission into commercial poultry. The arrival of H5N1 has changed the country’s approach from preparing for whether the virus will arrive to preparing for the possibility it becomes established among wild birds. Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard has already announced new regulations requiring poultry operations with more than 100 birds to develop, register and implement farm biosecurity plans covering avian disease. Those plans will need to address how farms prevent infection and what happens if disease is detected, including arrangements for humane culling, disposal, cleaning and disinfection. Operators will also face record-keeping and auditing requirements. The Government expects the regulations to come into force by the end of 2026. The poultry sector is particularly important to New Zealand’s food supply and economy. The industry generates an estimated $2.2 billion domestically each year and around $200 million in export revenue. That makes preventing major outbreaks important not only for farmers but also for consumers, food security and trade. The Government and poultry industry already have a formal agreement setting out how they will jointly prepare for and respond to serious exotic poultry diseases. Under that arrangement, the industry contributes 45 percent of general poultry disease readiness and response costs. For an H5N1 response, the industry contribution is 40 percent, with the Government meeting the remaining share of agreed response costs. The potential financial consequences are substantial. An earlier avian influenza outbreak at a commercial egg farm in Otago cost an estimated $25 million, despite being contained to a single property. That outbreak involved a different strain from the H5N1 virus now detected in New Zealand. The new support comes as farmers face the prospect of investing more heavily in farm infrastructure and disease prevention while maintaining the supply of chicken and eggs to New Zealand households. The challenge is particularly significant for smaller poultry operations, which may have fewer resources available to make rapid biosecurity improvements. For the Government, the objective is to strengthen those defences before H5N1 becomes widespread among wild birds and creates a constant infection risk for domestic poultry. With bird flu now inside New Zealand’s borders, biosecurity is no longer simply about keeping the disease out. news.content: Search analysis, research, academics... Home Arts + Culture Economy Education Environment + Energy Ethics + Religion Health Politics + Society Science + Tech World Podcasts Local En Español Edition Africa Australia Brasil Canada Canada (français) Català España Europe France Global Indonesia New Zealand United Kingdom United States Donate Skip to content Edition: United States Africa Australia Brasil Canada Canada (français) Català España Europe France Global Indonesia New Zealand United Kingdom s Donate Newsletters Become an author Sign up as a reader Sign in Academic rigor, journalistic flair Arts + Culture Economy Education Environment + Energy Ethics + Religion Health Politics + Society Science + Tech World Podcasts Local jared lloyd/Getty The first wave of bird flu is the worst: what Australia can learn from overseas Published: August 20, 2026 1:09am EDT Hundreds of dead birds are now being reported as the lethal H5N1 strain of bird flu begins to spread across Australia. Government reports show the virus is circulating in resident birds. It was a long time coming. The current outbreak emerged in 2020. By late 2021, it was spreading widely, leaving a widespread trail of devastation among wildlife species across Europe and the Americas. Even as Antarctic birds and mammals began suffering over 2024 and 2025, Australia – and New Zealand – remained free of this viral strain. Until now. It’s easy to picture bird flu as an unstoppable wave set to decimate Australian birds and mammals. But that’s not set in stone. Overseas evidence shows the first wave tends to be by far the worst. And deaths from the first wave can vary greatly, with many populations and individuals surviving. That’s good news for some – but it won’t save vulnerable species who may lose a large proportion of their global population. For them, recovery is likely to take decades – if at all. The first wave is devastating In 1996, a new highly pathogenic strain of bird flu emerged in poultry in China. Periodic outbreaks forced mass poultry culls and sporadic die-offs in wild birds. In 2020, a new variant – formally known as H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b – was detected. Soon, it was sweeping through Europe and North America. It was immediately clear the virus had become more devastating. Less dangerous strains of bird flu (termed low pathogenic avian influenza viruses) tend to replicate in a bird’s gastrointestinal tract, while earlier high pathogenic strains tended to replicate in the respiratory tract. But this new strain could infect both. Not only that, it was able to infect the central nervous system, leading to neurological disease and death. The strain has evolved many new variants since 2021. These can now infect over 500 wild bird species, of which over 50% had not had infections previously recorded. Then came reports of fatal infections in mammals, from scavengers such as foxes to herbivores such as deer and marine mammals such as sea lions. Many had never had bird flu before. The virus was even able to infect livestock such as cattle. Human infections are thankfully rare, with no reports of the virus spreading between people so far. Across western Europe and North America, deaths of breeding-age adult birds were as high as 25–76% in the worst-hit species. Many populations had near-complete breeding failures. In 2023, it hit South America. Some bird species lost up to 50% of their global population, while marine mammals suffered their first mass deaths. In Argentina, 17,000 elephant seals died in a single colony. The first wave of bird flu is often devastating. Pictured: dead cranes being removed in Germany in 2025. Christophe Gateau/picture alliance via Getty What happened next? While mass deaths of wildlife made global headlines, little media coverage has focused on what happened next. Mass deaths don’t seem to strike the same populations year after year, even though the virus is still circulating. Adult sandwich terns in western Europe died in droves in 2022. But in 2023, mortality rates in adults fell by 96%. That year’s chicks were hit hard, but those hatching in 2024 did far better. Why? Older, more vulnerable birds all died off in the first wave, and surviving terns gained some immune resistance. Younger birds previously shut out from breeding took advantage of the situation, while chicks benefited from reduced competition for food. Overall, sandwich tern numbers only fell modestly. Even so, the species is projected to take almost 20 years to recover to its pre-outbreak level. Not all populations or individuals were affected equally – even in the first wave. Atlantic seabirds breeding in large, dense colonies were hit hard. Gannets, terns and skuas all saw mass deaths. But neighbouring petrels, puffins and shearwaters nesting in burrows had far fewer deaths. This may give some protection to Australia’s burrowing little penguins. Authorities are also moving to vaccinate thousands of these penguins. For many species, bird flu is made worse by other threats. In 2024, Adéle penguins in Antarctica had to battle both bird flu and deadly avian cholera, leading to many losses. Similarly, bird flu hit African penguins already in trouble from the collapse of sardine fisheries. We can’t directly extrapolate from overseas experience. Many Australian birds and mammals are unique. Some, such as black swans, lack crucial immune defences against influenza. Removal of bird carcasses is one way to slow the spread of the virus. Pictured: workers removing dead birds from a Humboldt penguin reserve in Chile in 2023. Martin Bernetti/Getty The death toll is not set Official estimates suggest about 20% of bird and 10% of mammal populations in Australia are at high to extreme risk of population impacts from this strain. But catastrophic destruction is not guaranteed. Whether a species is hit hard or barely touched will depend on three things: level of exposure to the virus, how well it can resist infection and how well it can cope with being infected. Before this strain arrived, experts evaluated the risk for all Australian bird and mammal species, developed action plans for important sites and expanded surveillance and diagnostic systems to monitor outbreaks and viral evolution. These measures are globally recognised as the most important tools. Australia is now following New Zealand in vaccinating captive and closely-managed populations. Worldwide, no species has suffered 100% losses. That means some individuals likely survived the infection. Generally, animals can cope better with infection if they’re well fed, in a good habitat and aren’t exposed to pollution or stress. The biggest lever we can pull is tackling these other pressures, from habitat loss and plastic pollution to invasive species. We have a chance to try relieving these pressures on wildlife to give them more of a fighting chance – but the window is shrinking. Government reports show the virus is circulating in resident birds. It was a long time coming. The current outbreak emerged in 2020. By late 2021, it was spreading widely, leaving a widespread trail of devastation among wildlife species across Europe and the Americas. Even as Antarctic birds and mammals began suffering over 2024 and 2025, Australia – and New Zealand – remained free of this viral strain. Until now. It’s easy to picture bird flu as an unstoppable wave set to decimate Australian birds and mammals. But that’s not set in stone. Overseas evidence shows the first wave tends to be by far the worst. And deaths from the first wave can vary greatly, with many populations and individuals surviving. That’s good news for some – but it won’t save vulnerable species who may lose a large proportion of their global population. For them, recovery is likely to take decades – if at all. The first wave is devastating In 1996, a new highly pathogenic strain of bird flu emerged in poultry in China. Periodic outbreaks forced mass poultry culls and sporadic die-offs in wild birds. In 2020, a new variant – formally known as H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b – was detected. Soon, it was sweeping through Europe and North America. It was immediately clear the virus had become more devastating. Less dangerous strains of bird flu (termed low pathogenic avian influenza viruses) tend to replicate in a bird’s gastrointestinal tract, while earlier high pathogenic strains tended to replicate in the respiratory tract. But this new strain could infect both. Not only that, it was able to infect the central nervous system, leading to neurological disease and death. The strain has evolved many new variants since 2021. These can now infect over 500 wild bird species, of which over 50% had not had infections previously recorded. Then came reports of fatal infections in mammals, from scavengers such as foxes to herbivores such as deer and marine mammals such as sea lions. Many had never had bird flu before. The virus was even able to infect livestock such as cattle. Human infections are thankfully rare, with no reports of the virus spreading between people so far. Across western Europe and North America, deaths of breeding-age adult birds were as high as 25–76% in the worst-hit species. Many populations had near-complete breeding failures. In 2023, it hit South America. Some bird species lost up to 50% of their global population, while marine mammals suffered their first mass deaths. In Argentina, 17,000 elephant seals died in a single colony. The first wave of bird flu is often devastating. Pictured: dead cranes being removed in Germany in 2025. Christophe Gateau/picture alliance via Getty What happened next? While mass deaths of wildlife made global headlines, little media coverage has focused on what happened next. Mass deaths don’t seem to strike the same populations year after year, even though the virus is still circulating. Adult sandwich terns in western Europe died in droves in 2022. But in 2023, mortality rates in adults fell by 96%. That year’s chicks were hit hard, but those hatching in 2024 did far better. Why? Older, more vulnerable birds all died off in the first wave, and surviving terns gained some immune resistance. Younger birds previously shut out from breeding took advantage of the situation, while chicks benefited from reduced competition for food. Overall, sandwich tern numbers only fell modestly. Even so, the species is projected to take almost 20 years to recover to its pre-outbreak level. Not all populations or individuals were affected equally – even in the first wave. Atlantic seabirds breeding in large, dense colonies were hit hard. Gannets, terns and skuas all saw mass deaths. But neighbouring petrels, puffins and shearwaters nesting in burrows had far fewer deaths. This may give some protection to Australia’s burrowing little penguins. Authorities are also moving to vaccinate thousands of these penguins. For many species, bird flu is made worse by other threats. In 2024, Adéle penguins in Antarctica had to battle both bird flu and deadly avian cholera, leading to many losses. Similarly, bird flu hit African penguins already in trouble from the collapse of sardine fisheries. We can’t directly extrapolate from overseas experience. Topics & Projects Antimicrobial Stewardship Chronic Wasting Disease Osterholm Update Podcasts Newsletters About CIDRAP CIDRAP in the News Our Staff Our Director Osterholm in the Press Shop Merchandise Contact Us About Search Support Menu Cambodia confirms human H5N1 avian flu case as H5N1 hits more Utah egg farms News brief July 16, 2026 Stephanie Soucheray, MA Topics Avian Influenza (Bird Flu) Share mswine / Flickr cc Earlier this week Cambodian officials announced the country’s fifth human H5N1 avian flu case this year, this one involving a 9-month-old girl. The girl has been hospitalized and is receiving intensive care. So far no source of infection or exposure has been found, but the child’s close contacts are being given oseltamivir (Tamiflu) as a precaution. Cambodia reported 19 human cases of H5N1 in 2025, eight of which were fatal. Most recent cases in Cambodia have involved a reassortant (2.3.2.1e) between an older H5N1 clade that has circulated in Cambodia since 2014 and the newer clade 2.3.4.4b virus that is circulating globally. Utah reports H5N1 in poultry, cattle In US news, the US Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) reported for the second week in a row an egg farm H5N1 outbreak in Cache County, Utah, affecting 275,100 birds. In the past 30 days, 1.49 million birds have been hit with H5N1 in the United States. APHIS also noted several new detections of avian flu in cattle in Utah and Idaho, with each state reporting four confirmed cases this week. Twenty-six cattle in the past 30 days have been confirmed to be infected with H5N1, raising the year’s total to 81 cases. Moms who receive COVID, flu vaccines during pregnancy more likely to vaccinate their babies, study says News brief July 16, 2026 Meghan Holohan Topics Childhood Vaccines COVID-19 Influenza Vaccines Adult (non-flu) Vaccines Pressmaster / iStock Infants born to mothers vaccinated before, during, or soon after pregnancy for COVID-19 or flu were more likely to receive vaccines than those born to unvaccinated mothers, suggests a study published in Pediatrics. “The results show that maternal vaccination is strongly associated with infant vaccination in the first year of life, especially when vaccination occurred during pregnancy or shortly after delivery,” wrote the study’s authors, from Kaiser Permanente Northern California. “Improving maternal vaccine coverage during those times may improve child vaccine coverage, ensuring continuous protection in early life.” Implications for policymaking, intervention development The researchers looked at 82,533 mother-infant pairs in a retrospective cohort study of babies born from August 18, 2021, to March 31, 2024, to see how mothers’ vaccination status affected their babies’ likelihood of receiving flu or COVID-19 vaccines. The mothers of 32,370 babies (39% of the total) received a COVID-19 vaccine during pregnancy, and 43,806 babies (53%) were born to mothers who received a flu shot while pregnant. Improving maternal vaccine coverage during those times may improve child vaccine coverage, ensuring continuous protection in early life. If moms received a COVID-19 vaccine during pregnancy, their babies were 9.65 times more likely to also receive the COVID-19 vaccine. Moms who received a flu shot had babies who were 3.67 times more likely to also receive one. Babies had a 66.2% probability of getting a flu shot and a 23.4% chance of getting a COVID vaccine before they turned 1 year. “Our findings also suggest that some women may not be comfortable being vaccinated during pregnancy but are willing to vaccinate their infants; differences in attitudes toward vaccinating themselves vs their children have been observed in qualitative studies of parents, although not specifically around pregnancy,” the authors wrote. “Future studies examining the interplay of these factors will be an important part of making policy and developing interventions.” Most measles patients who sought care at Prisma Health in South Carolina were kids News brief July 16, 2026 Sarah Boden Topics Measles Most of the measles patients Prisma Health Greenville Memorial Hospital cared for during South Carolina's recent outbreak were kids aged 10 years or younger. NIH According to a letter from the health system's physicians, published yesterday in the New England Journal of Medicine, Prisma treated 81 people for measles from October 2025 to April 2026. A total of 997 cases were reported to the South Carolina Department of Public Health during the outbreak. The cases were concentrated in the Upstate region, particularly Spartanburg County, where measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccination coverage was 88.9%. The letter notes that at least 73% of those who sought care at Prisma were unvaccinated. Statewide, 93% of cases were among unvaccinated South Carolinians. The most common symptoms observed by Prisma clinicians were fever, cough or other respiratory symptoms, and the characteristic rash of flat red spots. Koplik spots, which are tiny, bluish-white clustered lesions on the inside of the mouth, were reported in a quarter of patients. Severe outcomes, lasting complications None of the 81 patients seen at Prisma Health died. Ten children and three adults were hospitalized, primarily for dehydration, respiratory problems, or pneumonia. Most hospitalized patients were sent home within 72 hours, though the report notes that two had prolonged hospitalizations due to measles encephalitis, a life-threatening inflammation of the brain. One of the two was discharged to an inpatient rehabilitation facility and "as of the time of this report is receiving ongoing outpatient therapy." The other patient recovered but continues to have headaches and a vocal tic. Within a month after being diagnosed with measles, 24 of the patients had concurrent or subsequent infections. analysis.event: Cambodia's Ministry of Health confirmed a fifth human H5N1 avian influenza case in 2026 involving a 9-month-old girl, who was hospitalized and receiving intensive care. analysis.brief_en: Cambodia confirmed its fifth human H5N1 avian influenza case of 2026 on July 16, involving a 9-month-old girl hospitalized in intensive care. Health authorities have not yet identified the exposure source, and close contacts are receiving oseltamivir prophylaxis as a precaution. In the United States, the USDA reported a fresh H5N1 outbreak at a Utah egg farm affecting 275,100 birds, part of a broader wave that has struck 1.49 million poultry in the past month. Concurrently, H5N1 detections in cattle expanded to Utah and Idaho, with 26 new cases in the last 30 days bringing the national total to 81 for 2026. Genetic sequencing in Cambodia suggests the virus is a reassortant clade (2.3.2.1e) derived from older Cambodian and globally circulating H5N1 lineages. No human cases have been linked to the U.S. animal detections.

analysis.time: Published 20 August 2026; event reported as occurring in the week preceding publication (not explicitly dated).
analysis.location_and_population: Australia; wild and domestic bird populations across multiple regions; no human cases reported.
analysis.event: Media report citing wildlife advocates warning that multiple mass mortality events in wild birds are suspected to be caused by avian influenza (bird flu). The report is preliminary and not confirmed by laboratory testing in the supplied evidence.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Approximately 1,000 dead birds reported across three mass mortality events; risk described by advocates as a sign of worsening avian influenza activity and potential broader ecological impact.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Under investigation; no official testing results, control measures, or public health response detailed in the evidence. Source notes advocates’ warning rather than confirmed outbreak status.

analysis.brief_en: Wildlife advocates have warned that three mass mortality events involving around 1,000 dead birds across Australia are suspected to be caused by avian influenza, describing the incidents as an ominous sign of escalating bird flu activity. The ABC report, published on 20 August 2026, cites advocates but does not provide laboratory confirmation or official case definitions. No human infections have been reported in connection with the events. Authorities have not released testing results, control measures, or public health guidance in the evidence provided, leaving the status of the suspected outbreaks unresolved. The report frames the events as preliminary and emphasizes the need for further investigation to confirm the cause and assess broader ecological risks.

The species is in the ‘high risk’ category of a government assessment of the potential effects of H5 bird flu. analysis.brief_en: A deadly H5 avian influenza strain circulating globally since 2021 has reached Australia, triggering mass mortalities among native seabirds and raising alarm for iconic species. Authorities report the first confirmed H5 death in a little penguin on Phillip Island and large-scale tern die-offs in South Australia and Victoria. Government risk assessments label silver gulls as high risk and Australian fairy terns—already listed as vulnerable—as very high risk, warning of possible severe population crashes. Experts cite the high mobility of seagulls and the scavenging and fish-eating habits of white-bellied sea eagles as key transmission pathways. In response, federal and Victorian governments have initiated vaccination programs for captive and wild birds, while acknowledging uncertainty about long-term impacts on native species encountering H5 for the first time.

news.content_zh: 自 2021 年以来在全球传播的致命 H5 禽流感 毒株已抵达澳大利亚,引发本土海鸟大规模死亡,并为标志性物种敲响了警钟。当局报告首次确认菲利普岛一只小企鹅因 H5 死亡,南澳大利亚和维多利亚州出现大规模燕鸥死亡事件。政府风险评估将银鸥标记为高风险,将已被列为易危物种的澳大利亚仙燕鸥标记为极高风险,并警告可能会出现严重的种群崩溃。专家指出,海鸥的高流动性以及白腹海雕的食腐和食鱼习性是 传播 的关键途径。作为回应,联邦政府和维多利亚州政府针对圈养和 野生鸟类 启动了 疫苗接种 计划,同时承认首次遇到 H5 对本地物种的长期影响存在不确定性。
